Privacy & cookies

Your data. Your house. Your rules.

I preach private AI, so this site practises it. Nothing that tracks you loads until you say yes, “Reject all” is one click, and you can change your mind any time.

Change cookie settings

Last updated 12 November 2026

The short version

  • One global standard: opt-in consent for every visitor, everywhere, before any analytics or advertising cookie is set.
  • Analytics (Google Analytics 4, Microsoft Clarity) and advertising (Meta Pixel, Google Ads) are separate choices. You can accept one and not the other.
  • Google Consent Mode v2 starts every visit at “denied”. Global Privacy Control is honoured as an opt-out of advertising.
  • I do not sell your personal information. I do not use cookies to make decisions about you.
  • Right now no analytics or advertising tags are switched on, so the site sets no tracking cookies at all. If that changes, this page and the cookie banner will tell you first.

Who is responsible

This website, youssefjalloul.com, is run by Youssef Jalloul (“I”, “me”), who is the data controller for the information described here. Contact for anything privacy-related: privacy@example.com. Work delivered through Inova AI Solutions is covered by Inova’s own privacy terms.

What I collect

  • Technical data your browser sends to any website (IP address, browser, device, pages requested), kept briefly in my host’s security logs.
  • Usage data, only if you accept analytics: pages viewed, clicks, scrolls and approximate location (country or city). Clarity masks text you type.
  • Advertising identifiers, only if you accept advertising: cookie IDs that let Meta and Google measure and target ads.
  • What you choose to share when you book a call through Calendly (name, email, notes). Calendly processes this under its own privacy policy.

Why, and on what legal basis

  • Running and securing the site: legitimate interests (and strict necessity for the consent record).
  • Analytics and advertising: your consent, which you can withdraw at any time.
  • Replying to you and holding a call you booked: taking steps at your request, and legitimate interests.

Your choices

  • Use Cookie settings at any time; it also sits at the bottom of every page.
  • Turn on Global Privacy Control in your browser and advertising stays off automatically.
  • Opt out at source: Google Analytics opt-out, Google ad settings, Meta ad preferences.

Your rights, wherever you are

European Union, EEA and Switzerland
GDPR, the ePrivacy Directive and Switzerland’s revised FADP. Non-essential cookies need your prior, opt-in consent. You can ask for access, correction, erasure, restriction, portability, object to processing and withdraw consent at any time, and complain to your local data protection authority.
United Kingdom
UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and PECR. Same rights as the EU. You can complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO).
United States
The California Consumer Privacy Act as amended by the CPRA, and comparable state laws (including Virginia, Colorado, Connecticut, Utah, Texas, Oregon and others). You can ask to know, delete and correct personal information and opt out of its “sale” or “sharing” for cross-context behavioural advertising. I do not sell personal information for money. Advertising tags may count as “sharing”, so they stay off unless you accept them, and a Global Privacy Control signal is treated as an opt-out. I will not discriminate against you for using these rights.
Australia
The Privacy Act 1988 and the Australian Privacy Principles. You can access and correct your information and complain to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC).
United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia
The UAE Personal Data Protection Law (Federal Decree-Law 45 of 2021), the DIFC and ADGM data protection regimes where they apply, and Saudi Arabia’s Personal Data Protection Law. You can be informed, access, correct and request deletion of your data, and withdraw consent.
Canada
PIPEDA and Quebec’s Law 25: consent for non-essential tracking, access, correction and withdrawal of consent.
Brazil, and everywhere else
Brazil’s LGPD, and similar laws such as Singapore’s PDPA, India’s DPDP Act, Japan’s APPI, South Africa’s POPIA and New Zealand’s Privacy Act 2020. Wherever you are, you get the strictest standard on this page: nothing that tracks you runs until you say yes.

Transfers, retention and security

Data may be processed in Australia, the UAE, the EU, the US and other countries where my providers operate. Where the law requires it, transfers rely on adequacy decisions, standard contractual clauses or equivalent safeguards. Analytics data is kept for no more than 14 months, consent records for as long as your choice applies, and booking details for as long as we are in conversation plus any period the law requires.

Children

This site is for professionals and is not directed at children. I do not knowingly collect children’s data.

Changes and complaints

If this policy changes in a way that affects your choices, the cookie banner will ask you again. To use any right above, email privacy@example.com; I reply within 30 days. You can also complain to your local regulator.
